podcast.title: Collaboration with Scarface
podcast.body: MF DOOM recently collaborated on an album with Scarface (Inspectah Deck), released about a month ago, which was highly recommended in an April release video. "ha sacado el disco en colaboración con MFDUM."

srcs.episode: Record Store Day 2018. Resumen de lanzamientos.

podcast.title: Constant Name Changes and Collaborative Nature
podcast.body: Throughout his career, MF Doom constantly changed his stage name, though most names contained "Doom" (e.g., Mr. Fud, Doom) or "Villain" (e.g., the villain). He was known for his extensive collaborations, with most of his albums being joint projects, and he worked with a wide range of artists both directly and indirectly. "ha cambiado de nombre, toda su carrera ha estado constantemente cambiando de nombre, casi todos tienen o el denominador comundum, MFDUM, MrFud, todo comdum o convilian."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Contemporary Graffiti Aesthetic
podcast.body: MF-DOOM is presented as a contemporary example of an artist who utilized graffiti as a means of political and artistic expression. "ejemplos más contemporáneos como MF-DOOM o Randy G-Wales dan prueba de ello."

srcs.episode: Cómo los Logos Definieron la Música ｜ Símbolos de Resistencia

podcast.title: Controversy Over Live Performances and Imposters
podcast.body: Throughout his career, MF Doom was highly controversial regarding his live appearances, giving very few concerts and being highly reclusive on stage, especially since signing with Lex Records. A significant point of contention was the frequent discovery that imposters, wearing his signature mask, would perform in his place at many concerts. Initially, he would claim it was him, perhaps thinner or not clearly visible, but eventually admitted to using stand-ins, leading to widespread anger and frustration among fans, with some imposters even being booed off stage. "una cosa que siempre ha generado muchísima polémica de mezón es que ha habido muchos conciertos bastantes conciertos en los que se ha descubierto que el que estaba saliendo a cantar no era el propio mezón sino que era otro tío y como le ponía la máscara de magneto esta que se pone todo el día nadie sabía que encoño era."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Creative Approach to Rap
podcast.body: MF DOOM is celebrated for his highly creative and unique contributions to the rap genre. He is considered one of the most imaginative and incredible figures in the history of rap. "mfdum hace como un montón de cosas como muy como muy especialmente creativas para ser de rap."

podcast.title: Dual Musical Style
podcast.body: MF Doom effectively bridges the gap between underground, experimental hip hop and more accessible forms, creating a unique sound that blends these often disconnected worlds. "es un exo muy interesante entre el hip hop underground, más de las profundidades o el hip hop más experimental y por el otro lado el hip hop más accesible."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Dual Talent as Rapper and Producer
podcast.body: MF Doom's comprehensive artistry stemmed from his equally strong abilities as both a rapper and a musical producer. "uno de las cosas que hace increíblemente completo a MFDUM es que es tan buen rapero como tan buen productor musical de hip hop."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Early Career and Resurgence
podcast.body: In his early career, MF Doom was part of a small, unsuccessful hip hop band with his brother. He later experienced a period of indigence in his twenties, living as a homeless person, before resurfacing as a major artist in underground hip hop under the name MF Doom. "en los inicios tiene una pequeña banda de hip hop con su hermano y con alguien más que no tiene mucho éxito. Después acaba prácticamente viviendo en la indigencia, acaba tirado viviendo como un indigente sin casa y ahí cuando tiene 20 pico años resucita como uno de los artistas, uno de los grandes artistas del hip hop underground, ya con el nombre de MFDUM."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: English-Peruvian Origin and International Life
podcast.body: MF Doom was an artist and producer of English-Peruvian origin. He spent much of his life in the United States and, at the time of recording, was living between the United Kingdom and the United States. "un artista de hip hop y productor de origen inglesper, que ha vivido todas en el estado sonidos, ahora vuelve a estar a camino entre el reino o unido y el estado."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Extreme Privacy and the Masked Persona
podcast.body: MF Doom was incredibly secretive about his personal life, giving very few interviews where he would only discuss his music, making him a "ghost" in the public eye. He consistently wore a distinctive mask, inspired by Magneto and comic book villains, which meant he was rarely seen physically without it, though he occasionally appeared unmasked in music videos or photos. "una persona increíblemente celoso de su vida y de su intimidad, sabemos muy poco de él, da muy pocas entrevistas, hay poquísimas entrevistas suyas en las que solo habla de su música."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Genius and Influence
podcast.body: MF Doom is regarded as one of the great geniuses and best artists in rap and hip hop history. His work is often recommended as an excellent entry point for those who may not typically enjoy rap music. "uno de los grandes genios del Kaviar, de uno de los mejores artistas del rap que es Mr. Doom MF Doom."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Innovative Use of Spoken Word Samples as Lyrics
podcast.body: A hallmark of MF Doom's career was his unique method of incorporating fragments of telephone recordings, movie dialogues, or news reports directly into his lyrics. Unlike other hip hop artists who might sample spoken words for musical elements, MF Doom used these audio clips as the actual lyrics, presenting them as if the sampled voices were singing the song, making the fragments the central argument of the track. "coge fragmentos de grabaciones telefónicas o de películas o de diálogos que encuentra y lo usa como letra y los pone y lo reproduce como casi como si fueran el cantante de la canción."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Jazz and Soul Influences in Production
podcast.body: His production style, particularly in rhythmic bases, drew heavily from jazz and soul influences. He directly incorporated rhythmic bases and musical structures from jazz, distinguishing his approach from artists like Wu-Tang Clan who might use deconstructed samples. This made his style similar to early breakbeat DJs who were inspired by jazz, like Eran Katkemi and DJ Fút. "En la parte de los basses rímpicas, en la parte de productor de música, tiene muchas influencias del jazz, del soul, pero a lo mejor no tanto como podían tener a mejor esbo tan clan que tenían esos trozos de construido, sino que realmente usaba ser rímpicas y estructuras musicales sacadas del jazz."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: MC Paul Barman Collaboration
podcast.body: MF Doom, referred to as "Emeth Dumb" in the transcript, collaborated on MC Paul Barman's album "Chamberland." "colaborado a Emeth Dumb."

podcast.title: Non-Aggressive Flow
podcast.body: Unlike many hip hop artists who use aggressive shouting, yelling, and swear words, MF Doom stands out for his lack of aggression. His flow is calm and measured, avoiding harsh endings to verses, often making him sound like he is reciting poetry rather than rapping, which appeals to a broader audience. "es un artista que no tiene esa agresividad, que a veces tienen muchos artistas de hip hop que a mucha gente que no le gusta el rap letir para atrás, estos artistas que gritan, que chican, que dicen tacos que son agresivos."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Performance Philosophy and Stage Fright
podcast.body: MF Doom addressed the controversy of using imposters by presenting a philosophical argument about the nature of musical performance. He asserted that the artist who composed, worked on, and directed the performance is the true performer, and his physical presence on stage is irrelevant because audiences come to hear the music and material, not to see him physically. He compared it to attending "The Marriage of Figaro" without expecting to see Mozart. Over time, he admitted that his actions were partly due to his significant fear of stages, which he believed would be understandable if properly communicated to the audience. "él está diciendo que realmente es el artista que ha compuesto que ha trabajado y que ha dirigido y que ha hecho el ha hecho la performance del directo y que él salga o no salga no es relevante porque la gente va a escuchar su música va a escuchar su material va a escuchar su gracio y no va a escucharla a él."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Representative of 21st-Century Experimental Hip Hop
podcast.body: MF DOOM is mentioned as an artist representing the truly experimental hip hop scene of the 21st century. "Nombres verdaderamente experimentales como puede ser [...] Mac Villain."

srcs.episode: Poniendo a Kanye West en su lugar

podcast.title: Revolutionary Poetic and Ironic Lyrical Style
podcast.body: As a rapper, MF Doom was revolutionary due to his distinctive writing style. He refrained from using excessive explicit language, instead preferring a more measured approach that heavily utilized irony and double meanings, often embedding two or three meanings within a single verse. His writing and flow were so unique that he was often compared to a poet. "su forma de escribir es muy característica. No dice tantísimas palabras más sonantes ni tantísimos tacos, es una persona en eso mucho más pausada, que además juega muchísimo con las ironías, con los doble sentidos, a veces sus versos tienen dos y tres significados a la vez y no lo oculta con lo cual estás como haciendo tres lecturas distintas de la misma lectura."

srcs.episode: MF DOOM. Repaso de un genio

podcast.title: Short Song Format Philosophy
podcast.body: MF Doom advocated for a philosophy in his music that emphasizes conciseness: "what you can say in two minutes, don't say in eight." This approach resulted in albums like Madvillainy featuring over 20 incredibly short songs, each with clear arguments and concise lyrics, in stark contrast to the longer, verse-heavy tracks common in rap. "la filosofía que siempre ha defendido el mezón es que lo que puedas decir en dos minutos no lo digas en ocho."
